reviewer.name: cursor-nov24-independent-hanshu-104 (Claude Opus 5.5)
reviewer.role: independent final identity reviewer (worker-authored repairs; require separate editorial review before application)

note: Definite English mistranslations/omissions found during the independent identity review. Not applied; source file unchanged. Identity approvals in the part reports rest on the Chinese source and do not depend on these edits.

repairs.zh: 魯人皆以儒教，而硃家用俠聞。
repairs.before: The people of Lu all took Confucian teaching, but the Zhu household became known by knight-errantry.
repairs.after: The people of Lu all took Confucian teaching, but Zhu Jia became known by knight-errantry.
repairs.reason: 硃家 is the Lu knight Zhu Jia (s0030 硃家，魯人; s0039 父事硃家; s0114), tagged as person hanshu:104:p028 in this unit, not a household or family.

repairs.zh: 魯人皆以儒教，而硃家用俠聞。
repairs.before: Lu was famous for scholars, yet the Zhu family made its name with swords.
repairs.after: Lu was famous for scholars, yet Zhu Jia made his name as a knight-errant.
repairs.reason: Same person as the literal field: 硃家用俠聞 says Zhu Jia became known for knight-errantry; 'the Zhu family' turns the named person into a lineage.

repairs.zh: 解姊怒曰：「以翁伯時人殺吾子，賊不得！」
repairs.before: Xie's elder sister angrily said: "In the days when Wengbo held sway, if someone killed my son, the culprit would not have escaped!"
repairs.after: Xie's elder sister angrily said: "In Wengbo's day someone kills my son, and the culprit is not caught!"
repairs.reason: 以翁伯時人殺吾子，賊不得 is the sister's reproach that, even with Wengbo (Guo Xie) at the height of his standing, her son's killer goes uncaught (cf. Shiji 124 以翁伯之義，人殺吾子，賊不得). The counterfactual past tense invents a contrast between a former and a present Wengbo.

repairs.zh: 解姊怒曰：「以翁伯時人殺吾子，賊不得！」
repairs.before: Guo Xie's sister raged, "When you still answered to the name Wengbo, no killer of my boy would have lived an hour!"
repairs.after: Guo Xie's sister raged, "With Wengbo as mighty as he is, a man kills my son and the killer goes free!"
repairs.reason: Same sentence: nothing in the source says Guo Xie stopped using the courtesy name Wengbo; the reproach is that his present standing has not caught her son's killer.

repairs.zh: 至若北道姚氏，西道諸杜，南道仇景，東道趙佗羽公子，南陽趙調之徒，盜跖而居民間者耳，曷足道哉！
repairs.before: As for the Yao gang on the northern road, the Du clans on the western, Qiu Jing in the south, the so-called Zhao Tuo princeling in the east, Zhao Diao in Nanyang—they were bandits in broad daylight, hardly worth ink.
repairs.after: As for the Yao gang on the northern road, the Du clans on the western, Qiu Jing in the south, Zhao Tuoyu Gongzi in the east, Zhao Diao in Nanyang—they were bandits in broad daylight, hardly worth ink.
repairs.reason: 東道趙佗羽公子 is rendered in the literal field and in accepted editorial decision r0011 as Zhao Tuoyu, courtesy Gongzi (person hanshu:104:p064); the idiomatic 'so-called Zhao Tuo princeling' drops 羽 and turns 公子 into a common noun, contradicting that accepted reading.

repairs.before: He fed the couple until they died.
repairs.after: He supported Lord Lü for the rest of the old man's life.
repairs.reason: 遂養呂公終身 names only Lord Lü (呂公, hanshu:104:p089); 'the couple' adds Old Lady Lü, who is not in this sentence, and 終身 refers to Lord Lü's lifetime.

repairs.zh: 涉由此怨王游公，選賓客，遣長子初從車二十乘劫王游公家。
repairs.before: Yuan She then sent his son Chu at the head of twenty wagons to sack Wang Yougong's house.
repairs.after: Yuan She therefore resented Wang Yougong; he picked out retainers and sent his eldest son Chu at the head of twenty wagons to sack Wang Yougong's house.
repairs.reason: 涉由此怨王游公，選賓客，遣長子初從車二十乘劫王游公家: the idiomatic field omits the resentment, the selection of retainers, and 長 'eldest' (the kinship claim for hanshu:104:p133 Yuan Chu rests on 長子初).

repairs.zh: 中叔子少游，復以俠聞於世雲。
repairs.before: Cao son Shaoyou won a knightly name in his turn, they say.
repairs.after: Cao Zhongshu's son Shaoyou won a knightly name in his turn, they say.
repairs.reason: 中叔子少游 means Zhongshu's son Shaoyou (father hanshu:104:p148 Cao Zhongshu, son hanshu:104:p150); 'Cao son' garbles the father-son relation.
